newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen says 80 pct of B share investors from HK.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen says 80 pct of B share investors from HK.

text.p: Some 80 percent of the B share investors on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in southern China are individuals or foreign institutions based in the former British colony of Hong Kong, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Monday.

Foreign currency B shares are technically restricted to foreigners -- including residents of Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan -- but many mainland Chinese are believed to have entered the Hong Kong-dollar denominated market via various channels.
Despite the figure given by the Shenzhen bourse-run newspaper, analysts have said mainland Chinese account for at least 50 percent of the market's daily trading turnover.
The newspaper, in a front-page article, also outlined several ideas on how to enliven trading of the B share market.
It said the stock exchanges in Shenzhen and Hong Kong could link their trading terminals and Shenzhen could promote secondary listings of some of its B shares in Hong Kong.
China could also allow some brokerage companies in Hong Kong, either foreign or Chinese, to conduct trading of A shares, which were now strictly reserved for mainland Chinese, it said.

The paper also said Hong Kong, which became a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1, could allow the secondary listing of some of its "China-concept" shares in Shenzhen but did not elaborate.

Other ideas included the establishment of joint brokerages, investment funds and accounting offices between the two cities and launching futures trading of one of Shenzhen's main stock indices in Hong Kong.
